annotations.title: You may haue societie.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> S. Iohn sheweth manifestly, that whosoeuer desire to be partakers with God, must first be vnited to the Churches societie, learne that faith, and receiue those Sacraments, which the Disciples receiued of the Truth it self, conuersant with them in flesh. So saith Venerable Bede vpon this place. Whereby we see there is no societie with God in sectes or schismes, nor any where but in the vnitie, fellowship, and communion of that Church which can proue it self to descend from the Apostles.

notes.text: No saluation but in the Societie of the Church.

annotations.title: The bloud of Iesvs.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> Whether sinnes be remitted by praiers, by fasting, by almes, by faith, by charitie, by sacrifice, by Sacraments, & by the Priests, (as the holy Scriptures do plainely attribute remission to euery of these) yet none of al these do otherwise remit, but in the force, by the merite & vertue of Christs bloud: these being but the appointed meanes & instruments by which Christ wil haue his holy bloud to worke effectually in vs. Which meanes whosoeuer contemneth, depriueth him self of the comoditie of Christs owne bloud, & continueth still in sinne and vncleannesse, vaunt he him self neuer so much of Christs death. Which point let the Protestants marke wel, and cease to beguile their poore deceiued folowers, persuading them, that the Catholikes derogate from Christs bloud, or seeke remission otherwise then by it, for that they vse humbly the meanes appointed by Christ to apply the benefite of his holy bloud vnto them.

notes.text: Many meanes & instruments of remitting sinne, but al by the force & merite of Christs bloud applied by them.

annotations.title: From al sinne.
annotations.text: ◦ From original and actual, venial and mortal, a culpa & pœna, that is, from the fault and the paine due for the same. V. Bede saith, that Christs Passion doth not onely remit in Baptisme the sinnes before committed. but al other afterward also done by frailtie: yet so, if we vse for the remission of them, such meanes as be requisite and as Christ hath appointed, whereof he reckeneth some. Bede vpon this place. See S. Augustine also vpon this place to. 9. and S. Hierome li. 2 con. Pelag. c. 3.

notes.text: Al remission of sinnes is by the Passion of Christ, though by secundarie meanes also.

annotations.title: That we haue no sinne.
annotations.text: [1] We gather by these wordes and the former, that there be two sortes of sinnes: one mortal, excluding vs from light and the societie of God: an other venial, which is found euen in those that walke in the light, and are in the societie of God. [2] Also we note against the Pelagians, that we be truely called the sonnes of God, and so iust in deede, though we be not without al sinnes, euery one of vs, as wel iust as vniust, being taught and bound to confesse our offenses, and to aske pardon daily of God, by this petition of the Pater noster, Forgiue vs our debtes. Therfore S. Augustine li. de natura & grat. c. 36. reckeneth vp al the holy Patriarches, Prophets, and renowmed iust persons, to haue been sinners, euen when they were in grace and iustice: [3] excepting alwaies our B. Ladie, de qua propter honorem Domini, nullam prorsus, cùm de peccatis agitur, habere volo quæstionem. of whom, saith he, for the honour of our Lord, when we talke of sinnes, I wil haue no question. And Pelagius asking what sinnes Abel & such iust men did commit, [4] [5] S. Augustine answereth, that they might laugh sometime immoderately, or iest to much, or couet somewhat intemperatly, or plucke fruite ouer greedily, or in eating take somewhat more then afterward was wel digested, or haue their intention in time of praier somewhat distracted, and such like. thus in sense S. Augustine. Whereby we may learne which be venial sinnes, that consist with true iustice & [6] can not alwaies be auoided euen of holy men in this life. In the booke de fide ad Petrum c. 41. are excepted from this common rule of sinners, the children which be newely baptized and haue not yet vse of reason to sinne either mortally or venially.

notes.text: A man may be truely iust, notwithstanding venial sinnes.
S. Augustine excepteth our B. Ladie from sinners.
